sections.overview: This coastal eastern Pacific sciaenid is commonly called the black croaker.
sections.identification: It has a deep dark body, a pale side bar, a black gill-cover mark and a heavy second anal spine.
sections.habitat: It lives near the bottom in rocky crevices and caves beside sandy areas, from 3 to 100 m deep.
sections.diet: Its recorded prey include mobile bottom-dwelling crustaceans, especially shrimp and crabs.
sections.behavior: A Southern California study found rocky-reef populations and large year-to-year changes in local abundance.
sections.reproduction: Gonad indices peaked in June and August, indicating late-spring and summer spawning.
sections.ecology: Its genus also includes C. fasciatum, but published records do not provide a reliable field comparison.
sections.conservation: The Smithsonian database reports Data Deficient status, and a 2008 study noted no species-specific fishery plan.
